interpretation: Refutes the leading hypothesis: with the entire backbone provably frozen/unchanged, LIBERO-Spatial got WORSE (73.33%->16.67%) not better. Re-diagnosis: action_encoder/head are shared weight matrices whose column/row ranges overlap between LIBERO (0-6) and RoboTwin (0-13) -- RoboTwin's gradient directly updates the same columns LIBERO depends on, and with the backbone frozen there is no downstream plasticity to compensate. Points to per-embodiment-separated projection weights (not a shared K=14 projection) as the next fix.

interpretation: Result contradicts the simple disjoint-offset-fixes-it hypothesis: with the same trainable-backbone treatment as exp0001, disjoint projection offsets should have produced retention >= exp0001's 73.33% if projection-column overlap were the sole interference mechanism. Instead it landed at 50.00%, worse than exp0001, better than exp0002. Per-task pattern is scattered/task-swapping rather than a uniform decline (3 tasks fine in exp0001 dropped to 0%, 3 different tasks weak in exp0001 hit 100%), consistent with either meaningful run-to-run variance on a small 3-trial/task panel or a new instability source from RoboTwin's all-fresh-init projection weights (vs exp0001's partial warm-start via reused/corrupted LIBERO weights). Combined with exp0002 (backbone freezing alone also failed), points toward the shared transformer backbone as an under-isolated interference channel -- no candidate so far has combined disjoint projections with a frozen backbone to test this cleanly. Recommends investigate-fastwam-problem before the next candidate.

interpretation: Completes the 2x2 matrix: overlap+trainable=73.33% (exp0001), overlap+frozen=16.67% (exp0002), disjoint+trainable=50.00% (exp0003), disjoint+frozen=63.33% (exp0004). Freezing the backbone has OPPOSITE effects depending on projection design: hurts with overlapping projections (73.33%->16.67%, no plasticity to compensate for projection corruption) but helps with disjoint projections (50.00%->63.33%, once projection corruption is eliminated, backbone drift becomes the dominant remaining interference channel and freezing removes it too). Confirms disjoint offsets are a real, substantial fix (huge 17%->63% jump isolated in the frozen-backbone regime) and that backbone-level drift is a second, independent interference channel. Still below exp0001's 73.33% and the 90% floor -- exp0001 (imperfect on both projection overlap AND full backbone plasticity) remains the best multi-embodiment retention result, suggesting backbone plasticity may provide some net-positive adaptation benefit that a full freeze forfeits, not yet isolated. task4 (bowl in top drawer) is 0% across every multi-embodiment candidate -- a persistently hard task independent of these design choices. RoboTwin progress check: click_alarmclock 33.3%/33.3% (clean/random) -- the first non-zero RoboTwin result anywhere in this project (exp0001 measured 0.0% everywhere including this exact task); adjust_bottle remained 0.0%/0.0%. Shows the frozen-backbone disjoint-offset recipe can produce real RoboTwin capability, not just avoid forgetting. Recommends exp0005 combine disjoint-offset projections with partial backbone plasticity (e.g. differential LR: much lower for backbone than projections) rather than a full freeze or full train.

evaluation_events.reference_checkpoint: exp0019 canonical 97.00%; 90% floor; every multi-embodiment candidate 16.67-73.33%

interpretation: DECISIVE FINDING: LIBERO-only continued training (zero RoboTwin exposure) degrades LIBERO-Spatial to 23.33% -- the second-worst result of any candidate in the project, worse than 6 of 8 multi-embodiment candidates. This falsifies the multi-embodiment-interference framing as the primary cause of the retention problem that drove candidate selection since exp0002 (projection overlap, backbone drift, mixing ratio). The real driver is a property of continuing to fine-tune this expanded/padded K=21/22 checkpoint, independent of RoboTwin presence. Leading hypothesis: cold-start Adam optimizer instability (weights-only resume means Adam moment estimates restart at zero, and bias-correction amplifies effective step size for the first ~10-50 steps against an already-converged solution) and/or the LR (3e-5) simply being too high for continued fine-tuning of an already-converged checkpoint. Recommends exp0010: same LIBERO-only setup at a 10x lower LR (3e-6) to directly test this.
modifications: No code changes -- new task config resuming the K=21/22 expanded checkpoint and training on LIBERO data alone (RoboTwin entirely absent from the mixture, not just down-weighted), using the existing libero_2cam_multiembodiment.yaml data config directly (plain single-embodiment RobotVideoDataset, no InterleavedEmbodimentSampler)

modifications: No training -- pure diagnostic. Ran LIBERO-Spatial candidate_screen directly on the raw K=21/22 expanded checkpoint with zero training steps applied, to test whether exp0001-exp0009 degradation predates training.

Iteratively eliminated two real confounds: (1) auto-computed multi-embodiment dataset_stats.json (1,712 episodes) mismatched vs exp0019 own paired stats (11,853 episodes, full reweighted mixture) -- fixed by using pretrained_norm_stats pointing at the original file; (2) embodiment_description text-conditioning, a Qwen-VLA-inspired mechanism added during initial multi-embodiment implementation and never part of FastWAM canonical eval, silently baked into the shared default config -- removed.

Found root cause via code inspection: research/tools/expand_checkpoint_for_multiembodiment.py randomly initialized new action_encoder INPUT columns; action_encoder input (noisy_action from flow matching) is genuinely non-zero at padded columns during both training and inference (unlike proprio, which is deterministically zero there), so random weights times real noise injected an untrained perturbation into the shared hidden representation on every forward pass. Fixed by zero-initializing those columns (matching the already-correct head output-row treatment).
why_this_might_help: User asked directly whether the padded/zero-training checkpoint was ever verified against the real eval harness; this had only been proven via synthetic unit tests, not a real LIBERO rollout.
what_to_watch: Whether re-expanding the checkpoint with the zero-init fix and re-running the same zero-training diagnostic recovers close to exp0019 inherited ~96.67-97.00%.

interpretation: Decisive: the LIBERO retention problem across exp0001-exp0009 predates training entirely. Zero-training eval on the raw expanded checkpoint already shows 23.33% (matching exp0009 fully-trained result almost exactly), falsifying the optimizer/LR-cold-start hypothesis from PROGRESS_0009 Section 9 (exp0010, never launched). Root cause: expand_checkpoint_for_multiembodiment.py randomly initialized new action_encoder input columns, which multiply genuinely non-zero flow-matching noise at padded positions on every forward pass -- an implementation bug in preservation of inherited action projection weights, not a training-dynamics or multi-embodiment-interference problem. Fixed by zero-initializing those columns. Two other real confounds also found and fixed along the way (dataset_stats mismatch, self-introduced embodiment_description conditioning never part of canonical FastWAM eval). Re-expansion with the fix in progress; a clean re-diagnostic is the next evidence point before any further training candidates.

Seed-variance test (seed=42 vs seed=100) resolved the mystery: exp0019-expanded jumps 73-75% -> 98% purely from a different random seed on Spatial, while release-expanded stays ~96-97% regardless of seed -- exp0019 has a narrow, seed-sensitive success margin specifically on Spatial (its own narrow final fine-tuning target), not a computational bug.
